segments:
Marcus Aurelius said this to himself
every single morning.

“The people I meet today will be
meddling, ungrateful, arrogant.”
Not to hate them.
To stop being surprised by them.
“None of them can hurt me.”

Expect the worst in people.
Stay kind anyway.
Save this for tomorrow morning.

Someone’s opinion of you
is living in your head rent-free.
Marcus Aurelius noticed something strange.

We love ourselves
more than anyone else.

Yet we trust their opinion of us
more than our own.
Why?

You are the only judge
whose verdict you have to live with.
Send this to someone who needs it.

You’re worried about something
that hasn’t happened yet.
Seneca wrote to a friend about this.

“We suffer more in imagination
than in reality.”

Most of what you fear
will never arrive.

And what does arrive,
you will meet with the same mind you have now.
Come back to today.
Follow for more Stoic rules.

You keep comparing yourself
to people online.
Seneca saw this 2,000 years ago.

“It is not the man who has too little,
but the man who craves more, that is poor.”

Their highlight reel
is not your measuring stick.
Run your own race.

Enough is a decision,
not a number.
Send this to someone who needs it.
